title: Racial Mix Consideration at Annual Primary 1 Registration
what_it_is: Racial Mix Consideration at Annual Primary 1 Registration

sections.label: Parental choice and multicultural learning
sections.summary: Parental choice in the P1 Registration Exercise affects schools' social profiles, while subjects teach students about Singapore's multicultural society.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Within this framework, parental choice during the P1 Registration Exercise impacts the social profile of students in our primary schools.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: In primary schools, students learn about living in a multicultural society through a range of subjects.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: In Character and Citizenship Education, students learn about the major cultures in Singapore, as well as ways to relate to people of different races and religions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: In Social Studies, students explore the contributions of different racial communities in the past and how Singapore’s past shaped the racial and religious diversity today.

sections.label: MOE cross-school interaction opportunities
sections.summary: MOE provides opportunities for students to interact with peers from different backgrounds within and across schools, such as through Co-Curricular Activities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) also provides opportunities for students to interact with peers from different backgrounds within and across schools, such as through our Co-Curricular Activities.
